ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 15665, as amended; Enforcement Decree, Presidential Decree No. 32705), Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality, and Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended). Beneficial ownership data is governed by FATF Recommendation 24 and must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and National Tax Service, with no public register access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notary Public certification at origin, then either (a) Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) for Apostille Convention member states, or (b) Consular Legalization at the embassy/consulate of the destination non-member state after MOFA authentication; the two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive, never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized representatives must be screened in real time against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the U.S. Commerce Department Entity List, and any designation published by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members, and close associates, are subject to enhanced due diligence in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12, requiring independent source-of-wealth verification, senior management sign-off, and continued monitoring. Automated screening runs must occur at least every 24 hours and on any trigger event, with negative news and adverse media monitoring, and a five-year audit trail of all screening results.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IROS) and the Electronic Court Registry System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, a corporate name must be composed in Hangul for statutory registration, but an English transliteration may be filed separately as a secondary trade name. The name is structured in four tiers: (1) the legal entity suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' or 'Stock Corporation', (2) the principal trade name, (3) the object clause of the business scope, and (4) additional identifiers to distinguish the company from identical existing registrations. Foreign word transliterations must follow the National Institute of Korean Language standards and must not create confusion with registered trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed company name, the applicant shall file a written objection with the competent district court registrar within fourteen (14) days from the rejection notice, stating the legal grounds and attaching a name search print-out. Upon a second rejection, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the Supreme Court Registry Office under the Administrative Appeals Act, or alternatively a revocation lawsuit before the Administrative Court within ninety (90) days from the final rejection. The appeal must include the original filing receipt, a corrected name search report, and legal arguments demonstrating non-confusion and compliance with the prohibited-token rules. Engaging local counsel is mandatory where the applicant is a foreign investor.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is deemed non-compliant for an entity licensed under IS

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288, 289, 291, 295, 312, 317, 318, 337 and 393; together with Articles 1 to 10 of the Framework on Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure for court registration filings; professional legal service practice additionally governed by the Attorney-at-Law Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court (or Local Court Support) having jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea; for a Seoul based entity, the Commercial Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and capital payment certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act. However, all subscribed shares must be fully paid in prior to the incorporation registration filing, and the bank's capital payment certificate must be issued from the capital subscription account. There is no blocked escrow account requirement for an ordinary commercial company; after registration, the paid-in capital may be used for corporate purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION

KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS that the first meeting of the board of directors (the Board) of [Company Name], a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea (the Company), was duly held at [Registered Office Address] on [Date] at [Time]. Due notice having been given or waived, and all directors being present, the chairperson declared that a legal quorum was present. After full deliberation, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and unanimously adopted:

1. Ratification of Subscribed Share Capital and Payment. RESOLVED, that the Board ratifies the share subscription statement annexed as Schedule A, showing the subscription of [Number] ordinary shares of the Company at a subscription price of [Amount] Korean Won per share, and acknowledges that each subscriber has paid in full the amount subscribed into capital deposit account number [Account Number] maintained at [Bank]. The Representative Director is directed to obtain the bank's certificate of payment, to file that certificate with the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court, and to prepare the shareholder register in accordance with Article 337 of the Commercial Act.

2. Adoption of the Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be and is hereby fixed at [Street Address, City, Republic of Korea]. The corporate seal, statutory minute book, shareholder register and all material corporate records shall be maintained at that office. The Representative Director is authorized to execute a lease for the registered office and to furnish the lease proof and landlord consent, if requested, to the registration court.

3. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer with sole signatory authority; [Name] and [Name] be and are appointed Inside Directors; and [Name] be and is appointed Auditor for the initial term prescribed by the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the incorporation registration application, to use the corporate seal and to represent the Company before all courts, banks, notaries, tax authorities and administrative agencies.

4. Banking and IOLTA Client Trust Account Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director, either alone or jointly with one other director designated by the Representative Director, is authorized to open and maintain general banking accounts and a segregated IOLTA or client trust account for cross-border commercial litigation and arbitration funds, to designate authorized signatories, and to execute wire transfer and account management agreements in compliance with the Financial Transaction Reports Act and anti-money laundering rules.

5. Authority to Complete Incorporation and Operational Filings. RESOLVED, that all acts taken by promoters or directors before this meeting to establish the Company are hereby ratified, and the Representative Director is directed to complete corporate registration, tax registration, professional practice licensing and any other regulatory filings necessary to commence business.

The foregoing resolutions were adopted by the unanimous affirmative vote of the Board and shall constitute binding corporate acts of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Founder Organizational Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public or notary commissioned by the Ministry of Justice; organization meeting conducted by the promoters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language containing the corporate name, corporate purpose, registered office, authorized and issued shares, share classes and transfer restrictions, method of contribution, board composition and auditor provisions. All promoters must execute the Articles before the notary with their identifiers and seals. The promoters then hold an organizational meeting to approve the Articles, appoint the first directors and auditor, and approve the capital subscription plan. If any promoter is a foreign resident, provide a valid passport and, if applicable, an Alien Registration Card; a power of attorney is required for any subscriber represented by an agent.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Promoter identification documents (passport or Alien Registration Card)
Organizational meeting minutes
Capital subscription schedule
Promoter list with share allocation and payment method
Power of attorney, if any promoter is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests modifications to the mandatory recitals or clauses, amend the Articles and re-notarize the corrected version before any filing. No court filing is made at this step, so the remedy is purely a correction and re-execution of the corporate instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Issuance of Bank Payment Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank branch in the Republic of Korea with foreign exchange capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital subscription account in the name of the promoters for the benefit of the proposed entity. Each subscriber must remit the full subscription price from a permissible source, and for foreign subscribers execute a foreign exchange declaration. The bank will confirm the aggregate deposit and issue a certificate of payment of capital, the statutory proof required by the Commercial Act. The certificate must state the account number, the account holder, the deposit date and the full paid-in amount. Funds cannot be released to the entity until incorporation registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Temporary capital deposit account application
Subscription schedule with bank remittance instructions
Foreign exchange transaction declaration for non-resident subscribers
Bank reference and source of funds documentation
Passport or ARC of each signatory
Completed capital payment certificate form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the source of funds, provide bank statements and audited source evidence; if the deposit is incomplete, the shortfall must be cured within one business day. If the foreign exchange declaration is rejected, re-file with a corrected purpose code for capital subscription before the bank issues the payment certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration Filing with Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court or Local Court Support having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed application for incorporation registration, notarized Articles, capital payment certificate, organizational meeting minutes, consents and identification of the newly appointed directors and auditor, and the registered office proof. The applicant must also submit a corporate seal certificate application and pay the registration tax and education surcharge. The court reviews the dossiers, enters the company into the commercial register, and issues a certified Certificate of Incorporation registering the entity as a Chusik Hoesa with limited liability as of the filing date.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration on the statutory form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of paid-in capital
Minutes of organizational meeting
Acceptance/consent letters of directors and auditor
Director and auditor identification documents
Lease agreement or registered office proof
Corporate seal registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, cure all deficient items within the period stated in the order, usually 7 days. If the application is rejected, file a new application after curing the defects or appeal the rejection through the non-contentious litigation procedure before the appellate court; urgent defects can be remedied by supplementary filing without a new application where permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Identification with National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of Korea, through the District Tax Office or Local Inland Revenue Office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days of incorporation registration, file the business registration application to obtain the permanent business registration number (corporate tax identification number). Complete VAT registration, withholding tax employer registration and the electronic tax invoice system registration. Provide the certified Certificate of Incorporation, articles, corporate seal certificate, office lease, and representative director identification. The business registration certificate is the operational license for general corporate activities and is also required to open final bank accounts and issue tax invoices.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Lease agreement for registered office
Representative director identification
Power of attorney if filed by a licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office withholds issuance pending verification of the place of business, submit additional lease deposit payment records or landlord consent. If the application is rejected for incomplete attachments, correct the submission and re-file the same day; the five-working-day processing period restarts only upon a complete filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Professional Legal Practice Authorization and Client Trust Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Bar Association and the Legal Business Division of the Ministry of Justice; commercial bank for the IOLTA account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the business scope is ISIC 6910 cross-border commercial litigation and arbitration, the entity must either hold or be affiliated with a licensed law firm established under the Attorney-at-Law Act before it may provide court representation or privileged legal advice. For the Chusik Hoesa structure, the first board must arrange for licensed Korean attorneys to become members, file the law practice authorization, and update the commercial registry if the entity converts to a legal professional corporation. Separately, open an IOLTA/client trust account for client funds, designating the attorney custodians and adopting conflict-of-interest and anti-money laundering procedures. If the business is limited to non-privileged asset tracing and litigation support, maintain professional indemnity insurance and restrict activities to avoid unlicensed practice.
required_dossiers: Attorney admission certificates of member lawyers
Korean Bar Association membership certificates
Law firm establishment authorization under the Attorney-at-Law Act
Commercial registry update documents (if entity type changes)
Conflict of interest and client trust account procedures
Corporate bank account application for IOLTA/client trust account
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Korean Bar Association or Ministry of Justice defers approval, cure the deficiency by appointing an admitted Korean attorney as director and statutory partner, and resubmit the authorization. During any suspension, the entity must limit operations strictly to non-legal cross-border commercial advisory services to avoid unauthorized practice penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for physical, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations; the professional regulator for ISIC 6910 legal activity is the Korean Bar Association and the Legal Business Division of the Ministry of Justice, with ordinary office occupancy regulated by the local municipal building authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable as an industrial license; the relevant operating authorization is the Law Firm Establishment Authorization under the Attorney-at-Law Act and the associated Business Registration Certificate under the Value Added Tax Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea (EIA supporting bodies: Korea Environment Corporation)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - ISIC 6910 legal services are a non-industrial professional office activity and are not listed in the scope of projects requiring a Prior Environmental Impact Assessment or Environmental Registration under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no manufacturing discharge points exist; office wastewater is discharged through municipal sewage, no point-source VOCs or hazardous waste streams are generated in litigation practice, and any paper or electronic waste is removed by a licensed municipal waste contractor.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office, obtain a fire safety certificate for office occupancy under the National Building Act and fire prevention standards; the local fire department conducts a periodic fire safety inspection and issuance of a fire safety management certificate is required before opening to employees and clients. A Civil Defense shelter designation is not applicable for ordinary office floors, but the building owner must maintain evacuation routes, emergency lighting and fire extinguishing equipment.

stage_2.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office, obtain a fire safety certificate for office occupancy under the National Building Act and fire prevention standards; the local fire department conducts a periodic fire safety inspection and issuance of a fire safety management certificate is required before opening to employees and clients. A Civil Defense shelter designation is not applicable for ordinary office floors, but the building owner must maintain evacuation routes, emergency lighting and fire extinguishing equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa, the company automatically becomes a domestic resident corporation upon incorporation and must complete VAT Business Registration (Value-Added Tax Act) and Corporate Tax registration at the district NTS office having jurisdiction over the registered office. File the Business Registration Application through the HomeTax portal or in person within 20 days of business commencement, together with the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, lease or ownership evidence of the Korean principal place of business, representative identification, and corporate seal registration certificate. The NTS then issues a 10-digit Tax Registration Number / VAT Business Registration Number (TIN/VAT ID) used for corporate tax, VAT, withholding, and customs declarations. A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean permanent establishment or branch must file a Foreign Corporation Domestic Place of Business Registration under the Corporate Tax Act and a parallel VAT Business Registration; required supporting documents include the foreign company registration certificate or equivalent, apostilled certificate of incorporation, board resolution authorizing the Korean branch, power of attorney, branch manager identification, and evidence of the Korean fixed place of business. If no Korean permanent establishment or fixed place of business exists, the foreign non-resident entity is generally not required to obtain a Korean VAT ID for outward-bound cross-border services; any Korean-sourced B2B service VAT may be handled by reverse charge by the Korean recipient.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korean law does not provide check-the-box or pass-through elections to a Chusik Hoesa. No hybrid mismatch election is available; group taxation is separately limited to resident corporation subsidiaries under the Corporate Tax Act and is not a pass-through election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory KRW turnover threshold under the Value-Added Tax Act; any business operator is mandatorily required to register for VAT from the commencement of business. Foreign non-resident entities with no Korean fixed place of business are not required to register for Korean VAT solely for outward cross-border services unless they create a taxable establishment or are otherwise required for specific imported service rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all business-to-business supplies under the Value-Added Tax Act. Issuers must transmit electronic tax invoice data to the National Tax Service through HomeTax or an NTS-approved EDI service provider; transmission must occur no later than the day following issuance. Each transmitted electronic tax invoice receives a unique NTS electronic invoice serial number for anti-fraud matching. There is no pre-clearance fiscal device blocking or physical digital stamping mandate; the real-time NTS electronic invoice database, automated matching with customs and foreign exchange data, and mandatory serial number system supply the anti-fraud control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods and qualifying exported services are zero-rated. Goods must be physically exported from the Republic of Korea and supported by a customs export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service. Services, including cross-border commercial litigation, arbitration advisory, and asset tracing services supplied by a Korean Chusik Hoesa to a foreign non-resident client, are zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident with no Korean business establishment and the service is properly characterized as an exported service, the consideration is paid in foreign currency, and the service is actually delivered to the offshore client with evidence of foreign exchange proceeds repatriated to Korea. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to foreign non-resident consumers are also zero-rated when the foreign-exchange and non-residency documentation requirements are met, and such zero-rating gives the Korean supplier the right to reclaim related input VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Receipt) accepted by Korea Customs Service, required only for physical goods or ancillary physical evidence shipments, filed through the UNI-PASS electronic customs portal
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, where physical goods or ancillary litigation exhibits are exported
Signed cross-border legal services agreement / client engagement letter evidencing the foreign non-resident recipient and the offshore nature of the services
Commercial invoice and zero-rated VAT tax invoice issued under the Value-Added Tax Act, carrying the zero-rated export supply indicator required by NTS electronic tax invoice data standards

Foreign Exchange Purchase/Repatriation Certificate or equivalent inward remittance certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, or a bank statement/foreign exchange registration record evidencing receipt of the export consideration in foreign currency
Copy of the foreign client's certificate of incorporation, permanent establishment non-residency evidence, or equivalent legal existence document

Evidence of service performance and offshore beneficial enjoyment, including engagement scope, work files, time records, arbitration or court filings, asset tracing reports, and electronic communications proving delivery outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may audit every zero-rated export claim by comparing VAT electronic tax invoice data, Korea Customs Service export declarations (for goods), service contracts, client non-residency evidence, and foreign exchange bank records of inward remittance within the statutory deadline. Where a zero-rated export is not fully substantiated or is found fraudulent, the NTS will reclassify the supply as a domestic taxable supply, assess VAT at 10% on the consideration, deny or claw back any input VAT refunds already released, and impose additional taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act, including penalties for false or dishonest tax returns (up to 40% of the evaded VAT for fraudulent non-reporting or underreporting) and late-payment interest under the National Tax Collection Act. Criminal prosecution is possible under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act for intentional VAT evasion, carrying imprisonment up to five years and fines up to three times the tax evaded; the statutory assessment limitation period is extended to ten years for egregious fraudulent evasion, and retroactive clawback can therefore reach all VAT and penalties for the full ten-year window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act administered in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a market-determined floating exchange rate with current account convertibility broadly free for trade, services, and ordinary business transactions. Capital account transactions are largely liberalized but remain subject to a declaration and filing regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Presidential Decree. Non-resident investors may freely remit dividends and profits, provided the overseas remittance is supported by tax payment certificates (e.g., corporate tax withholding certificate) and foreign exchange purchase evidence. Surrender requirements are minimal: exporters are permitted to retain foreign currency proceeds in domestic foreign currency accounts without mandatory conversion into KRW. However, banks must verify the source and underlying trade documentation to assign the correct Foreign Exchange Transaction Classification (e.g., code 600200 for trade receipts). Certain cross-border capital flows, especially when exceeding USD 100,000, may trigger reporting obligations to BOK/MOEF or require submission through the Customs declaration system. Overall, the regime is not a restrictive exchange-control system; it is better classified as a liberalized but prudentially monitored framework with emphasis on anti-money laundering, beneficial ownership disclosure, and tax compliance for profit repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected within the payment period stipulated in the trade contract (typically 120 days from the date of shipment, extendable under certain circumstances). There is no mandatory surrender ratio: all foreign currency export earnings may be credited to a domestic foreign currency account and retained indefinitely, or converted into KRW at market rates without requiring a specific conversion percentage. Banks must report each outgoing/incoming receipt in the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) via the Korea Customs Service or the banking network, assigning the applicable transaction code. Failure to repatriate within the contractual terms, or to submit the required export declaration (Cargo Clearance and Export Declaration), may trigger administrative penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI providers (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex) are not formally licensed as banks or electronic financial companies in South Korea under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. While they can offer multi-currency wallets and payment services to Korean entities through partnerships with local licensed banks, they cannot act as the primary settlement account for statutory capital verification, IOLTA-compliant trust accounting, or tax registrations with the National Tax Service. Their viability as a complementary rail is 'Low' for official treasury functions, but acceptable for operational spending where the funds are routed through a domestic partner bank. Korean regulators require every entity to maintain a domestic bank account for corporate seal-based transactions and tax filings; offshore EMIs generally fail this requirement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean banking law does not strictly mandate a physical in-branch appearance for all foreign directors, but the Financial Action Task Force-aligned Enforcement Decree to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires the bank to complete a face-to-face (or equivalent video-based) identification process if the entity is a foreign-invested company. Standard practice: at least one signatory director or an authorized officer (holding a board resolution and apostilled power of attorney) must attend a physical interview at the bank's corporate banking center. Remote notarial proxy opening is possible for certain bank accounts if the bank's compliance committee accepts a notarized, apostilled power of attorney plus a certified corporate registry extract; however, the 'one-time interview with a compliance officer' requirement is often accommodated via a video call satellite office of the Korean Consulate. In no event can the account be opened without the beneficial owner's identification and source-of-wealth questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) anonymity or incomplete chain disclosure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed UBO declaration in Korean (Real Form) and English, organizational chart showing ownership traced to a natural person, certified copies of share registers, capital contribution certificates, and apostilled passports. For trusts or holding structures, provide trust deed, certificate of incumbency, and a risk rating memorandum from a licensed corporate services provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border litigation and settlement flows as high-risk transaction sequencing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Retainer agreement, engagement letter, court/arbitration docket number, breakdown of expected case fee, counsel and expert budgets, and source of funds for the escrowed litigation war chest. The compliance committee will also request a sworn affidavit of the managing partner explaining the litigation funding structure and any third-party litigation funding agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions in the client/opposing party universe
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening results against UN/OFS/Korean Foreign Affairs trade control lists, sanctions and PEP check output of the full client list (for the banking network), as well as an in-house AML risk assessment report identifying any possible circumvention attempts. Provide correspondence of the court/arbitral institution to demonstrate that no forbidden jurisdiction is involved in the funds routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual foreign exchange conversions or non-business-related remittance patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Projected cash flow statement of the escrow account, a copy of the foreign exchange transaction declaration (K-Next / FEIS), and confirmation that every remittance will carry a disclosed purpose code and underlying contract. Where mirror trading is suspected, provide audited bank statements and a statutory auditor's comfort letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or litigation-war chest funds must be wired from the non-resident investor via SWIFT MT103 to the domestic KRW account or foreign currency account at the chosen Korean bank. The remitting bank must be instructed to include the purpose code '400100' (direct investment) or '400200' (indirect investment) as defined by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulation for capital receipts; for client funds held in trust, use code '410500' or appropriate service receipt code. The receiving Korean bank will complete a Korea Customs Service FEIS report within 1 business day and request the underlying certificate of incorporation, board resolution approving the investment, and for investments exceeding KRW 100 million, a notarized share subscription agreement. Capital verification (capital verification for paid-in capital) is performed by the external auditor (Samjung KPMG etc.) and recorded with the registry court; the bank will issue a 'Certificate of Foreign Currency Depository Balance' upon request.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for settlement, expert compensation, court filings, or litigation expenses are executed by SWIFT MT103 (international wire), domestic wire (K-Fast) for KRW, or, if the counterparty opens a letter of credit, a Commercial LC will be issued through the bank's trade desk. For recurring fees, an aggregated netting protocol with monthly payment instructions is recommended. Documentary collections are permissible for trade-related disbursements only; legal services usually settle against invoices via MT103 with supporting legal fee invoices and counterparty tax registration numbers. Standard purpose codes for outgoing service remittances are '300900' (legal services) or '300010'. All outbound remittances above USD 10,000 require the Foreign Exchange Transaction Form and the underlying contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (on-shore Korean won) for genuine current and short-term capital account exposure, subject to underlying transaction evidence and maturity not exceeding the underlying settlement date.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are restricted for Korean residents to offshore counterparties and require MOEF approval; onshore booking is generally not permissible.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps and FX swaps are allowed for asset-liability management when realigned with the actual currency risk profile, and prohibited for speculative purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting approval of financial statements, dividend declaration, and appointment or reappointment of external auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders meeting under the Korean Commercial Act; minutes kept at the registered office and, for any director changes, filed with the District Court Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year end, the ordinary general meeting must take place by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may face administrative fines of up to KRW 20 million for failure to hold a general meeting; uncertified financial statements cannot be filed, which cascades into tax return rejection and possible dormant-company strike-off by the National Tax Service after prolonged non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and taxable income schedule, including cross-border related-party disclosures and transfer pricing documentation if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year end, or within 3 months after the end of a non-calendar fiscal year; a one-month extension may be granted for audited financial statements subject to prior NTS approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% additional tax on underreported income, 40% for fraudulent concealment, 10% unfiled-return penalty, and daily overdue interest on unpaid tax at the statutory rate; prolonged non-filing results in NTS estimated assessment and administrative strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return covering the local income tax on the corporate tax base
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government, being the Metropolitan City, Province, City, County, or District, through the Local Electronic Tax System (LETS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the national corporate tax return, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Framework Act on Local Taxes imposes 20% or 40% additional tax for false or omitted local tax returns plus daily late-payment interest; continued default can trigger local government tax seizure and administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Signed statutory independent CPA audit report and audited financial statements for companies meeting mandatory audit thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service and Financial Supervisory Service through the External Audit Information System; also presented to the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At or before the annual general meeting approving the financial statements and filed with the authorities within two weeks after the annual general meeting; in no event later than the corporate income tax filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a statutory audit or to submit the audit report is an offense under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; directors and auditors may be fined, and the NTS may disregard unaudited financial statements and reassess tax with 20% or 40% underreporting penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 following the end of the fiscal year for companies registered as foreign-invested companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late reporting is subject to a fine of up to KRW 3 million; prolonged non-compliance may lead to revocation of foreign-invested company registration and loss of tax benefits, visa, banking, and administrative privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual compliance confirmation for licensed legal practice and professional indemnity insurance for ISIC 6910 legal services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Bar Association and, if applicable, the Ministry of Justice for foreign legal consultants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the license anniversary date; where the practice entity is an attorney-owned Chusik Hoesa, confirmation is aligned with the March 31 annual general meeting cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlicensed practice is a criminal violation under the Attorney-at-Law Act; the Korean Bar Association may suspend the responsible attorney, and the entity cannot lawfully render litigation or commercial arbitration services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and verification of the shareholders' register, directors' and auditors' registers, charges register, and minute books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretary and board of directors; the related director-change registrations are filed with the District Court Registration Office within the statutory two-week window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the annual general meeting date, i.e., March 31 for a December fiscal year end, and upon any share transfer or director change; court registration changes are due within two weeks of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain registers exposes directors to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act, loss of evidentiary weight of the records, and suspension of shareholder rights enforcement; deliberate destruction may create liability for unfair corporate conduct.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its subsidiary decree, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory where the company falls within any of the following categories at the preceding fiscal year-end: (a) total assets of at least KRW 10 billion, approximately USD 7.6 million; (b) total liabilities of at least KRW 5 billion, approximately USD 3.8 million; (c) 100 or more full-time employees; (d) 500 or more shareholders; or (e) listed status on the KRX or a specially regulated financial or investment license. In addition, an entity with total assets of at least KRW 120 billion, approximately USD 91 million, is classified as a large stock company and is subject to audit committee formation, quarterly review, and auditor designation. Companies below the thresholds remain exempt unless the articles of incorporation, lender covenants, or foreign parent consolidation require a certified audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are required for listed corporations and for unlisted large stock companies designated by law. Non-listed Chusik Hoesa may prepare statutory financial statements under K-GAAP, including the small and medium enterprise accounting standards within Korean GAAP. Cross-border litigation entities with trust, escrow, or IOLTA-equivalent client account activity must apply the applicable Korean accounting framework consistently and disclose any foreign parent consolidation differences.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not impose a standalone annual UBO return on a private Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is verified through banks and financial institutions on an ongoing basis under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act and FATF-aligned AML procedures. Any transfer of shares becomes effective against the company only after entry in the shareholders' register; the company should update the register within 30 days from receipt of the transfer notice to avoid defective records. If the transfer changes the representative director or directors, a court registration application is due within two weeks under the Korean Commercial Act. For foreign-invested companies, the annual MOTIE/KOTRA report captures controlling foreign shareholding and must also be updated within 30 days after a reportable change. A prudent recurring confirmation protocol re-verifies the UBO schedule at each annual general meeting and before each dividend or escrow payment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges, Mortgages, and Charges
Minute Book of Ordinary and Extraordinary Shareholders' Meetings
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings
General accounting books and supporting vouchers required by the Korean Commercial Act

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $800 - $2,500 per annum, depending on registered office services, corporate secretary support, and local attorney or licensed accounting agent coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 - $18,000 per annum for a non-listed Chusik Hoesa; fees increase for consolidated or large-stock-company audits, IFRS or K-IFRS conversion, and cross-border litigation escrow accounts

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax rate (progressive: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax, producing an aggregate headline rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax Incentive Limitation Act mechanisms may apply, including R&D tax credits (up to 50% of qualifying R&D expenditure for SMEs), employment promotion tax credits, and investment-related credits for Free Economic Zone (FEZ) and Foreign Investment Protection Act projects; however, cross-border commercial litigation and arbitration chambers generally do not qualify for patent-box or offshore free-zone profits, so the effective tax rate will approximate the statutory rate unless carefully monetising R&D/employment credits associated with litigation technology and case-management infrastructure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporation Tax Base and Tax Return, known in Korean as suo - 법인세과세표준및세액신고서) - official national tax form for the Chusik Hoesa, accompanied by schedules for foreign tax credit, transfer pricing, and non-resident withholding; filed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing portal at www.hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual presumed corporate tax prepayment declarations are required by August 31 for trading profits of the first six months
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months from the entity's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year filer, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year; if the three-month period falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deadline extends to the next business day

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate identity and fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, corporate legal name (Chusik Hoesa), statutory representative, current fiscal year, entity at-risk classification, and jurisdiction of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every non-resident direct shareholder, their nationality, tax residence, shareholding percentage and any controlling foreign parent; for a Chusik Hoesa with non-resident ownership above certain thresholds, attach the non-resident shareholder schedule and declare whether the entity is engaged in a Korean trade or business for treaty purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Accounting net income before tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income per Korean GAAP or K-IFRS financial statements, including worldwide revenue before tax adjustments; for litigation chambers, this includes arbitration fees, success fees, settlement management fees, and IOLTA trust bank interest earned.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean resident corporation is taxed on worldwide income; however, foreign-source income attributable to a foreign permanent establishment may be excluded or subjected to foreign tax credit; careful allocation must be made between Korean-sourced legal advisory income and offshore asset-tracing income, so the tax return must be accompanied by an account-level profit-and-loss schedule for each overseas engagement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax adjustments, additions and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter all tax-adjustment items, including non-deductible expenses (entertainment over-limits, fines, illegal political payments), nondeductible reserves, tax-exempt income, and provisions reversed in the current year; special attention is given to litigation-related accrued success fees and contingent liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border commercial litigation, fees paid to foreign co-counsel must be economically substantiated with time sheets, engagement letters, and bank wire records; payments to nominee or conduit consulting companies are non-deductible and will be recharacterised; likewise, IOLTA trust-account funds are not taxable as corporate revenue except for interest and any fee-sharing element.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Taxable base and progressive bracket computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the final taxable income after tax adjustments and apply the progressive corporate tax rates (9%, 19%, 21%, 24%) to arrive at the computed national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean Chusik Hoesa remains the taxpayer; no look-through treatment applies to treaty shareholders. If a non-resident shareholder has equity participation giving rise to foreign treaty provisions, ensure that the entity-level corporate tax is not reduced by applying dividend treaty rates at this box. Provide statutory reconciliation if the entity has claimed excluded foreign permanent establishment income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Foreign tax credit and foreign-source income exclusion
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report foreign income taxes paid or accrued on foreign-source litigation revenue and compute the foreign tax credit allowed under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA) Article 21, subject to the global foreign tax credit limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach certified customised foreign tax receipts, certified translations, and a Tax Residency Certificate where reliance is placed on a foreign tax authority's certificate; the foreign tax credit is limited to the Korean tax attributable to foreign-source income and cannot offset Korean domestic source income; failure to timely certificate the foreign taxes received will result in deletion of the credit and imposition of additional tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Transfer pricing disclosure and local/master file confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of whether the Chusik Hoesa engaged in transactions with foreign related parties above the statutory threshold; identification of related-party loan and service transactions and the prescribed transfer pricing method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The box requires attaching the TP documentation summary (Local File and Master File) and confirming arm's length treatment of intercompany fees paid to foreign affiliated law practices; for a litigation practice, cross-border service charges for dispute analytics, expert witnesses, and settlement counsel must be supported by operating expense schedules and functional risk analysis; penalties for a false entry here can reach 30% of understated tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest and royalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recap of withholding amounts imposed on payments to non-resident recipients of dividends, interest, and royalties, together with treaty claims for reduced withholding or exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Chusik Hoesa acts as withholding agent and must pay the aggregate withholding tax (20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge = 22%) unless a DTA relief application has been approved; the approved DTA relief must be evidenced by the NTS exemption/reduction certificate; the exact statute and treaty article must be cited in the attached Schedule for Non-Resident Income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Reserves, provisions and special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-deductible reserves (bad debt, retirement, litigation-related reserves, construction warranties), special tax concessions, and any disallowances of accrued foreign tax penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a commercial litigation chamber, IOLTA client trust liabilities cannot be claimed as corporate liabilities except for actual escrow obligations; reserve calculations must track Korean GAAP; because the entity provides cross-border litigation services, all foreign value-added taxes or foreign surcharges claimed as deductions must be supported by a foreign tax invoice and should be analysed for VAT deductibility in Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2, late filing of the corporate return attracts a penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax where unpaid tax does not exceed KRW 50 million, rising to 30% above that threshold; fraudulent or grossly negligent underreporting attracts an additional penalty of 30% of the evaded tax; Article 47-3 imposes a daily-delinquency surcharge on unpaid tax, currently calculated at 0.022% per day from the statutory deadline to the actual payment date; willful evasion is a criminal offence under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment of up to 10 years and a fine of not less than two times and not more than five times the tax evaded, and the NTS may also blacklist the entity and obtain a travel ban order against its statutory representative.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding when a Korean Chusik Hoesa pays a dividend to a non-resident shareholder: 20% national income tax under Article 125(1) of the Income Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surcharge (10% of the national tax); this aggregate may be reduced under an applicable Double Tax Agreement, typically to 15% on portfolio dividends and 10% on dividends received by a treaty-partner corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting capital; no additional Korean corporate tax is levied on the distributing corporation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief for dividend, interest, or royalty outbound payments, the non-resident recipient must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction, issued within 6 months of filing; the Chusik Hoesa and the recipient must jointly submit the 'Application for Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax on the Income of Non-Resident or Foreign Company' (Form SNT-1) to the district tax office having jurisdiction before the first payment to the non-resident; the application must attach: (i) the TRC original or apostilled copy; (ii) a Beneficial Ownership Statement evidencing the recipient's entitlement to the income without a conduit/back-to-back arrangement; (iii) a copy of the relevant DTA and ownership certificate; (iv) if corporate shareholder, a share register demonstrating qualifying holding percentage; after administrative review (normally 3-4 weeks), the NTS issues an approved exemption/reduction certificate, which must be retained in the taxpayer's records and attached to the annual corporate return; if approval is not obtained before payment, the full 22% must be withheld and the non-resident may seek a refund through the appeal and revision process within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest paid to a non-resident: 22% aggregate (20% national + 2% local); statutory withholding on royalties for the use of intangible property: 22% aggregate; under Korean double tax treaties following the OECD Model, treaty-dependent rates are generally 10% for interest and 10-15% for royalties (e.g., US-Korea: 10% interest, 15% royalties; Japan-Korea: 10% interest, 10% royalties for industrial royalties; China-Korea: 10% interest, 10% royalties); for cross-border commercial litigation, payments for copyrights in case-management software, know-how, and database licensing are treated as royalties, while payments for legal consultation are services subject to no general WHT but may be recharacterised as royalties if significant IP transfers occur; related-party royalty payments must also satisfy the arm's length standard and the substantive economic substance doctrine under LCITA and Korean GAAR.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File documentation under Article 6-2 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs arises when a Korean domestic corporation has annual gross revenue of KRW 100 billion or more and cross-border transaction values with foreign related parties exceed KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year; a fuller Master File obligation applies where the intercompany transaction amount exceeds KRW 50 billion; Country-by-Country Reporting threshold is for a multinational group with consolidated revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more; for lower-turnover litigation chambers, contemporaneous TP documentation is still strongly recommended where foreign affiliated lawyer bills are deducted, and the NTS can impose penalties of up to 30% of the understated tax for failure to produce documentation within 60 days.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 17-2 contains a strong general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) and Korea's tax courts apply 'substance over form' extensively; in cross-border commercial litigation and asset tracing, the Korean Chusik Hoesa must prove that its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are performed in Korea - key attorney decisions, client acquisition and retainership management, arbitration strategy formulation, risk assessment, settlement authority, and international execution of foreign judgments - otherwise the NTS may reattribute profits to a foreign principal, disregard a sham foreign branch, or deny treaty benefits under the OECD Principal Purpose Test. Expected records include fee earning schedules mapping each foreign collection matter to specific Korean case managers and supporting core activity documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting foreign settlement proceeds, arbitration award income, or cross-border asset-tracing commissions from accounting records; creating fictitious foreign legal-service invoices to load deductible expenses; submitting false Box 5 foreign tax credit claims; using IOLTA trust accounts to park corporate revenue while describing disbursements as client advances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-2 and 47-3 impose penalty taxes of 30% of the evaded amount plus daily delinquency surcharges; Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 punishes tax evasion with imprisonment for up to 10 years and a fine of not less than 2 times and not more than 5 times the amount of tax evaded; the NTS may treat the transaction as a sham and apply the substance-over-form doctrine to disregard the shell intermediary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly approved the fraudulent return is subject to personal criminal prosecution as a joint principal; Korean courts frequently pierce the corporate veil under the abuse of corporate personality doctrine to hold directors civilly liable for the entity's unpaid taxes and related damages; the NTS can impose a travel ban (blacklisting) on the director under the immigration enforcement rules and seize personal bank accounts, foreign real estate, and trust distributions up to the amount fraudulently removed; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment of up to 10 years plus a fine and disqualification from serving as a director of any Korean company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Failure to Maintain TP Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging or paying extraordinary fees to a foreign affiliated law partnership or litigation-funding vehicle at above-arm's length rates; creating evidence of deceased intercompany time-sheets; failing to submit the mandatory Local File/Master File despite crossing the KRW 5 billion intercompany transaction threshold; shifting profit from Korean litigation services to a low-tax offshore counsel entity without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA) Article 8, the NTS may reallocate income by its own arm's-length method and impose an additional tax penalty of up to 30% of the understated corporate tax; Article 13(3) provides a penalty for failure to submit TP documentation of up to 10 million KRW or 5% of the transaction amount; for severe manipulation, the GAAR provisions in the Framework Act may disallow loss deductions and recharacterise the foreign entity as a sham; the statutory daily surcharge continues for each day of non-payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signatory to the non-arm's-length contract becomes a specially liable person; Korean insolvency jurisprudence allows the court to pierce the veil if the director intentionally depleted the corporation to the detriment of the tax authority; the director may be personally ordered to make restitution of the transferred fee amount plus statutory interest; a tax-driven travel ban can be imposed, and if the NTS proves a criminal design the director faces imprisonment of up to 5 years for violation of LCITA, in conjunction with the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Failure and Misuse of Client Trust (IOLTA) Accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Committing a commercial litigation chamber client trust funds or cross-border settlement proceeds to direct operating expenses; failing to conduct respective customer due diligence on beneficial owners of overseas corporate clients; intentionally failing to report during wire transfers above the KRW 10 million threshold; using the IOLTA account as a conduit for inbound proceeds originating from an illicit foreign transaction or sanctions-flagged jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Korea AML Act) Article 12, failure to file a suspicious transaction report is subject to a criminal fine of up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment for up to 5 years; Article 11 imposes imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million on legal practitioners who abet money laundering through professional services; the Financial Information and Analysis (FIU) may impose a corrective order, revocation of the attorney-at-law license, and blacklist the firm from accepting further client transfers; aggravated penalty provisions can double the sanction if the funds are traced to organised crime or foreign bribery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for knowingly structuring the misuse of the client trust account; Korean criminal courts have pierced the corporate veil to force director-level asset confiscation, and the FIU coordinates with the Prosecutor's Office to obtain travel bans and freezing injunctions on personal and corporate assets; a director convicted of AML facilitation faces imprisonment of up to 5 years, a personal fine, civil disgorgement of all trust funds diverted, and permanent disqualification from practising as a litigation counsel in Korea.
